title: Principles of Earned Autonomy: A Governance Framework for Autonomous Agents
description:
What this is. Principles of Earned Autonomy (PEA) is a proposed theory-level governance framework for how autonomous AI agents may earn, exercise, and lose authority.

Claimed contribution. The contribution is the synthesis, not the isolated claims that reasoning matters or self-narration is unreliable: two core problems, three architectural principles (Operator's Intent, Observable Autonomy, and Convergence Is Silence), and one proposed measurable property, Autonomous Reasoning Fidelity (ARF), are combined into a discipline of earned, observable, revocable authority.

v2.4.0 additions. This version propagates substrate-general framing to the main digest surfaces, adds an AAS-1 assertion mapping and public-comment material, adds an ACS deployment case study, and aligns current references with Agent Cognition Skills (ACS) and Agent Evidence Proxy (AEP).

Evidence posture. Public evidence remains bounded. ACS supplies a developer-tooling reference lineage with model-family-diverse convergence and recorded falsification. AEP supplies an independently authored, fail-closed capture boundary for buffered traffic. The initial ARF dataset was administered through the historical LLM Harness Protocol v2.0.0; it is not attributed to AEP v0.1.0, and ARF independent replication remains open. PEA is not presented as a complete solution to AI safety, reasoning correctness, or autonomy.

Read in this order. README.md, PROBLEM.md, PRINCIPLES.md, then PROOF.md. EMPIRICAL_EVIDENCE.md is background and corroboration rather than part of the core evidentiary line.

Canonical source. GitHub repository. The broader research stack is anchored by Augmented Individual Intelligence (AII), and reference implementations include Agent Cognition Skills and Agent Evidence Proxy.
